user.title: Price sensor
user.description: Pair one all-inclusive dynamic price sensor with a currency. Every appliance added to this entry is costed against this price at the moment of consumption.

data_description.price_sensor: All-inclusive price per energy unit, for example EUR/kWh or EUR/MWh. The integration converts units but never adds fees, VAT, or margins — this sensor is the only price authority.
data_description.currency: Must match the price sensor's unit numerator exactly. The currency is immutable after creation: to change it, remove this entry and add it again (a mixed-currency cost series would corrupt statistics).

confirm_no_statistics.title: No hourly statistics for this price sensor
confirm_no_statistics.description: {price_sensor} does not declare state_class: measurement, so Home Assistant records no hourly mean statistics for it. Live costing works; the historical backfill will not. Submit to continue anyway.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure price sensor
reconfigure.description: Change the price sensor of this entry. The currency is immutable: to change it, remove this entry and add it again (a mixed-currency cost series would corrupt statistics).

data_description.price_sensor: All-inclusive price per energy unit, for example EUR/kWh or EUR/MWh. The integration converts units but never adds fees, VAT, or margins — this sensor is the only price authority.

error.price_sensor_unavailable: The selected price sensor is unavailable. Its current state is needed to validate the unit; try again when it has a value.
error.price_not_numeric: The price sensor's state {state} is not numeric.
error.price_unit_unsupported: The price sensor's unit {unit} is not supported. Expected a per-energy price such as EUR/kWh, EUR/MWh or EUR/Wh.
error.currency_mismatch: Price unit numerator {numerator} does not match currency {currency}. This integration never rescales prices (a subunit price like snt/kWh would be 100x off) — point it at a sensor in {currency}/kWh or {currency}/MWh.

abort.already_configured: A config entry for this price sensor already exists.

preview_backfill.name: Preview backfill
preview_backfill.description: Dry run of the historical cost backfill: reads the hourly long-term statistics of the entry's price sensor and appliance energy sensors and returns per-appliance point counts, totals and gaps. Writes nothing — importing is a separate, explicitly confirmed action. An ok result means the source data passed validation at preview time; the import separately enforces overlap protection and re-reads history. Price history is interpreted in the price series' current unit; if the price sensor's unit changed mid-history, older previewed figures are wrong — sanity-check the totals.

config_entry.name: Config entry
config_entry.description: The Appliance Energy Cost entry whose appliances are previewed.

start.name: Start
start.description: Start of the period, inclusive. Must be a top-of-the-hour UTC instant; a value with a timezone is converted to UTC, a value without one is interpreted in the Home Assistant timezone, and after conversion minutes, seconds and microseconds must be zero.

end.name: End
end.description: End of the period, exclusive. Same top-of-the-hour UTC rule as start; must be after start and not in the future. Defaults to the start of the current UTC hour, so a partial hour is never included.

appliances.name: Appliances
appliances.description: Limit the preview to the appliances using these energy sensors. Default: every appliance in the entry. Also the recovery path when one appliance's missing statistics fail the whole call.

strict.name: Strict
strict.description: When on, ok is false if any appliance has missing-price or invalid-energy hours, so findings must be resolved or consciously accepted before importing. When off, ok stays true and the findings are reported only in the per-appliance counts and ranges.

period_not_top_of_hour.message: {field} must be a top-of-the-hour UTC instant (minutes, seconds and microseconds zero); got {value}.

end_not_after_start.message: end must be after start; got start {start} and end {end} in UTC.

end_in_future.message: end must not be in the future; got {end}, now is {now} in UTC.

unknown_appliances.message: No appliance in this entry uses these energy sensors: {entity_ids}.

appliance_subentry_damaged.message: Appliance {subentry} is not usable: its configuration does not decode or its cost sensor is missing from the entity registry. Repair or remove the appliance, or exclude it with the appliances filter.

price_sensor_no_statistics.message: The price sensor {price_sensor} records no long-term statistics; it needs state_class: measurement. Without hourly mean prices no historical cost can be reconstructed.

price_statistics_unit_unsupported.message: The stored statistics unit {unit} of price sensor {price_sensor} is not a supported per-energy price unit. Expected a unit such as EUR/kWh or EUR/MWh.

price_statistics_currency_mismatch.message: The stored statistics unit numerator {numerator} of price sensor {price_sensor} does not match the configured currency {currency}. This integration never rescales prices.

appliance_no_statistics.message: Appliance {appliance} has no long-term statistics for its energy sensor {energy_sensor}, so no historical cost can be reconstructed for it. Exclude it with the appliances filter to preview the others.

energy_statistics_unit_unsupported.message: The stored statistics unit {unit} of appliance {appliance}'s energy sensor {energy_sensor} is not supported. Expected Wh, kWh or MWh.

user.title: Add appliance
user.description: Name the appliance and pick its existing cumulative energy sensor. The appliance's cost sensor prices consumed energy at the price in force at the moment of consumption.

data_description.name: Display name for the appliance and its cost sensor.
data_description.energy_sensor: An existing cumulative energy sensor in Wh, kWh or MWh with state_class total or total_increasing. Only energy this sensor has already measured is costed.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure appliance
reconfigure.description: Rename the appliance or swap its energy sensor. Swapping keeps the accumulated cost and re-baselines from the new sensor's current reading.

data_description.name: Display name for the appliance and its cost sensor.
data_description.energy_sensor: An existing cumulative energy sensor in Wh, kWh or MWh with state_class total or total_increasing. Only energy this sensor has already measured is costed.

error.energy_sensor_unavailable: The selected energy sensor is unavailable. Its current state is needed to validate the unit; try again when it has a value.
error.energy_unit_unsupported: The energy sensor's unit {unit} is not supported. Expected Wh, kWh or MWh.
error.energy_not_cumulative: Only cumulative energy sensors (state_class total or total_increasing) can be costed; a power or per-period sensor would corrupt the figures.
error.energy_not_numeric: The energy sensor's state {state} is not numeric.
error.duplicate_energy_sensor: {other_appliance} already uses this energy sensor in this entry.

abort.already_configured: An appliance for this energy sensor already exists in this entry.
